criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Mission purpose, rationale and single-satellite choice are well argued with references. Operator and customers are vague, relying on 'would likely' and example agencies rather than a defined operator. Some intro claims lack citations, such as the population reliance statement. Sits at the top of Adequate.

evidence.quote: The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM) for research and/or education.

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Most required elements are present, with STK access tables, a J2 inclination plot, and a classical element table. Errors weaken it: RAAN is wrongly tied to launch site, access rows 14 and 15 are duplicated, and the EOL choice contradicts itself. criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: The conclusion summarises the design and notes launch risk and the Vega C fallback. It is largely a restatement and does not draw evidence-based conclusions on EOL, manoeuvres or access performance. Some claims, such as the reef-protection outcome, are speculative.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Headings and a contents list give structure. However there is a truncated sentence, garbled reference entries, and a Wikipedia source. Figures and tables are not numbered or captioned consistently, and there are many spelling and grammar errors such as 'purposed' and 'complied'. Presentation impedes reading in places.

technical_issues.issue: RAAN is described as indicating the launch facility location, which is incorrect. RAAN is an orbital plane orientation, not a site location.
Access summary lists the same 13:00:32.812 pass twice (access 14 and 15), so the statistics and total duration are inflated.
Claims two launch windows per day because site latitude is below target inclination. This reasoning is not supported and is not a valid criterion for launch windows.
Perturbation calculations are referenced in the executive summary but no equations or hand calculations are shown.
States uncontrolled descent is the sensible choice, then says a passive strategy is required, and the drag sail option is cut off mid-sentence. The EOL decision is unclear.
Wikipedia is cited as a source, contrary to course rules; several references are incomplete or garbled, with no access dates.

overall: Solid, relevant preliminary design with STK access data and a reasoned orbit choice, but notable technical errors (RAAN, duplicated access rows), unclear EOL and launch decisions, missing hand calculations and weak references including Wikipedia. Presentation has many errors and unnumbered figures.

feedback.summary: You have produced a relevant, well-structured preliminary design. Your mission rationale is clear, your orbit choice is reasoned, and you include STK access data, which together earn an Adequate standard. Technical errors and unresolved decisions are holding the report back, particularly the RAAN description, duplicated access records, the launch window reasoning and the end-of-life choice. Correcting these, showing your calculations and tightening references would move your work toward Accomplished.

criteria.C1: Your introduction clearly states the primary mission, why it is needed, and why a single spacecraft was chosen, with supporting references. To reach the top band, define your operator and customers precisely rather than relying on 'would likely' and example agencies. Add citations for claims such as the population reliance statement.
criteria.C2: You cover most required elements: launch site and vehicle, a classical element table, a J2 inclination plot, and STK access tables. Errors reduce the standard. RAAN is wrongly linked to the launch facility, the 13:00:32.812 pass appears twice, and the launch vehicle choice shifts between Vega VV18, Vega E and Falcon 9. Perturbation and hand calculations are referenced but not shown, and your EOL decision is inconsistent.
criteria.C3: Your conclusion summarises the design and notes launch risk and the Vega C fallback, but it mostly restates earlier sections. Draw specific conclusions from your evidence, such as what the corrected access data shows about communications and why your EOL method suits the orbit. Remove speculative claims, such as the reef-protection outcome, unless you can support them.
criteria.C4: Your report has a logical structure with headings and a contents list. Improve readability by proofreading for spelling and grammar (for example 'purposed' and 'complied'). Number and caption all figures and tables consistently, and repair garbled or incomplete reference entries. Ensure every in-text citation matches the reference list.

next_steps: Correct the technical errors: fix the RAAN description, remove the duplicated 13:00:32.812 access row and recalculate the access statistics, and justify a single launch vehicle choice.
Show your perturbation and hand calculations with equations, and make one clearly justified end-of-life decision (passive or drag sail) supported by evidence.
Replace Wikipedia with peer-reviewed or agency sources, complete every reference with access dates, and proofread the document while numbering and captioning all figures and tables.
